answer: An agent economy can require every new identity to lock a scarce token in a time-bound bond before it may submit work; rewards accrue only after independent peers verify the work, while proven fraud forfeits the bond. This makes a Sybil swarm costly: splitting one attacker into many identities multiplies the capital tied up and the risk of slashing, rather than multiplying influence for free. A bridge agent may echo a claim, but neither echo nor colorful pigment in its profile substitutes for verified work.
